pr_title: Videoio: FFMpeg remove locks from `VideoCapure/VideoWriter::open()` to fix 20114
pr_body:
Remove locks added in https://github.com/opencv/opencv/pull/9006 from `VideoCapure/VideoWriter::open()` when using the FFMpeg backend to fix https://github.com/opencv/opencv/issues/20114.

Locks are removed if `OPENCV_FFMPEG_IS_THREAD_SAFE==true`.

Should I add a test?  If so it would need to be skipped on Windows to avoid build bot failures and it may be confusing when it fails on user's machines?

issue_context.title: Windows FFMPEG back end VideoCapture::open() blocks VideoCapture::open() and VideoWriter::open() in other threads
issue_context.body:
On windows when opening up RTSP streams with VideoCapture::open() and the FFMPEG back end, there is normally a delay, say 2000ms while the stream is setup, which is to be expected.
While this is happening any additional calls to VideoCapture::open() and VideoWriter.open() in other threads are blocked.
Is this blocking/queuing part of OpenCV or FFMPEG and can it be removed?

##### System information (version)
- OpenCV => 4.5.2
- Operating System / Platform => Windows 64 Bit
- Compiler => Visual Studio 2019

comments:
There are two kind of locks used in OpenCV-FFmpeg backend:
* Internal FFmpeg locks set via `av_lockmgr_register` (https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/6265155ce42de26146c5e9578f6e5518aa78de49/modules/videoio/src/cap_ffmpeg_impl.hpp#L867)
* Locks in `open` methods: https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/6265155ce42de26146c5e9578f6e5518aa78de49/modules/videoio/src/cap_ffmpeg_impl.hpp#L880 and https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/6265155ce42de26146c5e9578f6e5518aa78de49/modules/videoio/src/cap_ffmpeg_impl.hpp#L2410

We can try to reduce scope of the second kind of locks or remove them completely, test videoio_ffmpeg.parallel should check if it works https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/6265155ce42de26146c5e9578f6e5518aa78de49/modules/videoio/test/test_ffmpeg.cpp#L242
If FFmpeg spend these 2000ms in a single non-thread-safe function (e.g. `avcodec_open2`), then there is not much we can do on our side to reduce delays.

Also, in recent versions of FFmpeg `av_lockmgr` mechanism is deprecated (https://ffmpeg.org/doxygen/4.1/group__lavc__misc.html#ga4e9a0032df8f76cc766846514cebfab7) and seem to be removed in the _trunk_ version (https://ffmpeg.org/doxygen/trunk/group__lavc__misc.html), instead FFmpeg must be built with "thread support". Perhaps this should be investigated too, maybe Windows plugin build scripts should be changed.

Thank you for the quick reply.  I checked the removal of the two locks (AutoLock lock(_mutex);) and that solves the issue, passes TEST(videoio_ffmpeg, parallel) and doesn't appear to cause any problems.

Does TEST(videoio_ffmpeg, parallel) passing 100% guarantee that this is thread safe?

Passing test does not guarantee safety, usually thread-related problems can be reproduced only once in a multiple test runs or in certain conditions like busy system. This test and lock-mechanism are quite old (https://github.com/opencv/opencv/pull/164) and there is a chance these workarounds are not required anymore for modern FFmpeg versions. There are mentions that it uses internal locking now and can be considered thread-safe in most configurations (https://lists.ffmpeg.org/pipermail/libav-user/2014-August/007298.html).

Our FFmpeg plugin for Windows is built with threading support: https://github.com/opencv/opencv_3rdparty/blob/ead6edd2bea1e31275f8a4d756cd068f8034af9a/ffmpeg/make_mingw.sh#L119

I think we can try either to remove locks but only for newer FFmpeg versions, either provide an environment variable to control locking mechanism in runtime (enable it by default). Maybe @alalek can suggest something else.

With the lock in `VideoCapture::open() `
https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/6265155ce42de26146c5e9578f6e5518aa78de49/modules/videoio/src/cap_ffmpeg_impl.hpp#L880
removed, `VideoCapture::open()` sometimes fails due to `avformat_open_input` returning  [AVERROR_EXIT](http://ffmpeg.org/doxygen/trunk/group__lavu__error.html#ga334ea23fd9e492cd0e718330f2353b6b).  I don't know enough about FFmpeg to ascertain why, but I guess the removal of the lock is not a good idea without some additional checks.

I could only test this on an FFmpeg build from November last year as it looks like OpenCv [needs a few updates](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/issues/20147) to be compatible with the latest version.

@mshabunin From your previous comment related to

> 2017-12-26 - a04c2c707d - lavc 58.9.100 - avcodec.h
>   Deprecate av_lockmgr_register(). You need to build FFmpeg with threading
>   support enabled to get basic thread-safety (which is the default build
>   configuration).

and as the OpenCV windows FFmpeg shared library is now using `libavcodec == 58.134.100`, could we disable the mutex for versions of OpenCV built against libavcodec >= 58.9.100?

@cudawarped , do you mean `lockmgr`? I believe it is already removed: https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/3c76b335326283cdadbde1df21e9cf307fa338f8/modules/videoio/src/cap_ffmpeg_impl.hpp#L107-L110
Or do you mean internal `AutoLock` calls?

> Or do you mean internal `AutoLock` calls?

The `AutoLock` calls (introduced in https://github.com/opencv/opencv/pull/9006), which cause all calls to `VideoCapture::open()` into a que.  I'm still getting failures in my testing with 10+ threads with FFmpeg > 5 when the mutex is removed but I suspect it may be the compilation options used in the FFmpeg libraries I'm linking to.  

Weirdly I haven't managed to find the documentation relating to thread safety in FFmpeg or exactly what compiling with the below flags
```
--enable/disable-w32threads --enable/disable-pthreads
```
guarantees.

I've tested `--enable-pthreads` and `--disable-pthreads` on Linux. Removing `AutoLock` seem to have no effect when threading support is enabled (will be auto-detected if not explicitly disabled), but the `parallel` test crashes when FFmpeg is built without threading support and `AutoLock` guards are removed in OpenCV.

Windows FFmpeg plugin is built with `--enable-w32threads` option, but since it is cross-compilation in Linux container I'm not 100% sure it actually have been enabled. Probably it can be verified using `avutil_configuration()` function or something like this (https://ffmpeg.org/doxygen/trunk/group__lavu__ver.html). Could you please check it on a Windows machine?

Other thing is that even if we remove locks on our side we must be sure FFmpeg is built with threading support (better at runtime because dynamic library can be replaced by another). So the robust check should be developed before we remove safeguards or at least an environment variable (e.g. `OPENCV_FFMPEG_THREAD_SAFE=0`).

> Windows FFmpeg plugin is built with `--enable-w32threads` option, but since it is cross-compilation in Linux container I'm not 100% sure it actually have been enabled. Probably it can be verified using `avutil_configuration()` function or something like this (https://ffmpeg.org/doxygen/trunk/group__lavu__ver.html). Could you please check it on a Windows machine?

The flags from the most recent build of the Windows FFmpeg plugin (https://github.com/opencv/opencv_3rdparty/tree/ffmpeg/4.x_20221225)

> --       avcodec:                   YES (58.134.100)
> --       avformat:                  YES (58.76.100)
> --       avutil:                    YES (56.70.100)
> --       swscale:                   YES (5.9.100)
> --       avresample:                YES (4.0.0)

include `--enable-w32threads` (full output of `avutil_configuration()`) below.

> --enable-cross-compile --arch=x86_64 --target-os=mingw32 --cross-prefix=x86_64-w64-mingw32- --pkg-config=pkg-config --enable-static --enable-avresample --enable-w32threads --enable-libopenh264 --enable-libvpx --disable-filters --disable-bsfs --disable-programs --disable-debug --disable-cuda --disable-cuvid --disable-nvenc --enable-libaom --prefix=/build/ffmpeg_x86_64/install

Now I just need to run some tests on this build to see if there are any threading issues when calling `open()`.

I'm still getting failures when calling `CvCapture_FFMPEG::open()` from 5 different threads.  Sometimes with the following error
```
incorrect codes
Assertion ret >= 0 failed at libavcodec/bitstream.c:287
```
from
https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/blob/e30302c63638b0dfc5ba4bc60146c44d4af5ce40/libavcodec/bitstream.c#L226

This is with `AutoLock` removed when OpenCV is built:
1) With the Windows plugin compiled with `--enable-w32threads`, 
> --     FFMPEG:                      YES (prebuilt binaries)
2) Against pre-built windows libs from https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/releases which are compiled with `--disable-win32threads` and `--enable-pthreads`
  > --     FFMPEG:                      YES (find_package)

Do you think I am expecting too much from what FFMpeg calls "basic thread-safety"?

Did you try to run `opencv_test_videoio --gtest_filter=*parallel*`? Maybe thread-safety also depends on particular codec being used?

I think we can add environment variable which disable locks, so that it would be possible to improve performance with "safe" platform/container/transport/codec.

I was running my own thread test but I can confirm that unfortunately `opencv_test_videoio --gtest_filter=*parallel*` also fails on my Windows system when the locks are removed.  It doesn't always fails on the first run but if I place the call in a loop
```
FOR /L %%A IN (1,1,100) DO (
  opencv_test_videoio.exe --gtest_filter=*parallel*
  if errorlevel 1 (
   cmd /k
  )
)
cmd /k
opencv_test_videoio --gtest_filter=*parallel*
```
I can always get a failure.

I'm going to try it on the same hardware in Linux.

I've tried it on Ubuntu 20.04 with the latest version of FFMpeg and v4.2.2 and I don't get any errors when using the default config (no pthreads flag) or when specifying `--enable-pthreads` and I get a different error to Windows when I explicitly disable threading with `--disable-pthreads`

Linux Error with `--disable-pthreads`
> [mpeg4 @ 0x7f7424001dc0] ac-tex damaged at 40 18
> [mpeg4 @ 0x7f7424001dc0] Error at MB: 1210

Windows Error with `--enable-win32threads` or `--disable-win32threads  --enable-pthreads`

> incorrect codes
> Assertion ret >= 0 failed at libavcodec/bitstream.c:287

In both cases I am only making a single change, removing the lock for `VideoCapture::open()`
https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/4ed07411c3be7e8bf99a5c23698f4df47ae393a5/modules/videoio/src/cap_ffmpeg_impl.hpp#L1007

I am not sure why it doesn't work in Windows but we could still disable the lock here if a user requests it.  If that is the case:
1) Should this be an an environmental variable which affects all calls or an extra param which could be configured per call to `open`?
2) Is there any point in validating the FFMpeg version and/or return value from `avutil_configuration()` or should it be the responsibility of the user who has disabled the lock?

My opinion:
1. Yes, we can add an environment variable
2. No, it should be user's responsibility to determine that FFmpeg/codec/container/transport combination they use is thread safe.

@asmorkalov , @opencv-alalek , what do you think?

review_comments: Will this make any difference if the the scope of `threadSafe` is limited to `isThreadSafe`?

It depends on what we need.
- `static` - make variable with "global" lifetime and execute rhs expression once
- no `static` - read configuration on every call. We should not do that for performance sensitive cases, but there is no performance problem in the current case.
